{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   -J solov2-tissuenet-n-2C
#   -A sada-cnmi
#   -p tier3
#   --time=120:0:0
#   --error=%x_%j.err
#   --output=%x_%j.out
#   --mem=200G
#   --gres=gpu:a100:4

flux alloc \
  -n 1 \
  --gpus=4 \
  --time=120h \
  --queue=tier3 \
  bash -lc '

# NOTE: Slurm -A sada-cnmi (account/project) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but accounting/charging/allocation association may be incorrect.

# NOTE: Slurm --mem=200G has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: Slurm --gres=gpu:a100:4 requests a specific GPU model (a100).
# Flux has no universal, portable directive for GPU type; only the count (--gpus=4) is requested.
# Performance implication: you may be scheduled on non-A100 GPUs, affecting performance/compatibility.

# NOTE: Slurm %x (job name) and %j (job id) substitutions in output/error filenames are Slurm-specific.
# Flux does not provide portable equivalents in the batch script.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but log naming/organization may be degraded.
# Best-effort: use fixed jobname string and Flux job id.
exec >"solov2-tissuenet-n-2C_${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>"solov2-tissuenet-n-2C_${FLUX_JOB_ID}.err"

# NOTE: Slurm job name (-J ...) is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

spack load cuda@11.0.2%gcc@9.3.0/lrd2rcw
cd mmdetection
nvidia-smi

sh mmdetection/tools/dist_train.sh mmdetection/configs/solov22C/solov2_r50_fpn_60e_coco_tissuenet_n.py 4 --work-dir /shared/rc/spl/mmdet_output/All_to_all/nuclear/SOLOv2
'
"
}
